historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case Y1-Y5 average (9.0/7.5/6.5/5.5/4.5), anchored to FY2026 delivery guidance (~870 vs 793) and the A320 rate-75 / A350 rate-12 ramp; equity CAGR rejected as a growth proxy
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (26% 3yr, 32% 5yr) diverges far above revenue (7.7%/8.0%) and EPS (7.0%) because equity is recovering from the FY2020 COVID trough (EUR 6.4bn) and FY2022 hedge-reserve lows; it measures balance-sheet repair, not growth capacity, so it is not used. 5yr revenue CAGR is also flattered by the 2020 base (FY2019 to FY2025 is only +0.7%/yr).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-5.4%, FY2022 ~3,529 to FY2025 2,988) is well below reported FCF (+1.8%): SBC roughly tripled (115 -> 333) and interest income on the EUR 27bn gross cash pile rose from ~180 to 710, so an increasing share of reported FCF is treasury yield and stock-paid comp rather than operating cash. FY2022 interest income is estimated (~180) from the 9M 2022 run-rate of 92. FY2020 owner FCF was negative (-7.1bn reported), so 5yr FCF and EPS CAGRs are undefined. CAGRs computed on fiscal years to 31 December.

scenario_narratives.base: Airbus works through a ~9,200-aircraft backlog that is supply- rather than demand-constrained. Deliveries rise from 793 (FY2025) to ~870 (FY2026 guidance, reaffirmed July 2026) and toward ~990 by 2028 as A320-family rate 75 and A350 rate 12 are reached, then growth decays to traffic-like 2.5-3%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin climbs from 13.0% to 15.5% (EBIT ~10.8%) on final-assembly leverage, services mix and a restored Defence & Space margin; cash tax normalises from 16% to 24% as deferred-tax assets are consumed; capex settles near 4.4% of revenue plus lease renewal. Working capital is neutral. The axes that decide which scenario materialises are (1) engine availability from Pratt & Whitney and CFM, (2) rate-75 industrial execution incl. the integrated Spirit sites, (3) EUR/USD on the ~40% unhedged dollar revenue, and (4) Defence & Space charge discipline.
scenario_narratives.bull: Engine supply normalises in 2026-27, deliveries reach ~1,000 by 2028, A321XLR/A350F win share from a Boeing still fixing MAX 10 and 777X, European rearmament lifts Defence & Space to a 7-8% margin and the space JV removes the satellite losses; pre-SBC EBITDA reaches 17% and growing PDPs make working capital a small cash source.
scenario_narratives.bear: The GTF/LEAP shortage persists, FY2026 deliveries land near the bottom of guidance and rate 75 slips two years; under-absorption, tariffs and a stronger euro pin EBITDA near 13%, Space/A400M charges recur, inventory keeps absorbing cash, and COMAC erodes Chinese single-aisle demand from 2030 so terminal growth is 2%. Net cash keeps this a value-erosion case rather than a solvency case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House basis: owner FCF with IFRS 2 share-based payment expensed, interest income on the EUR 23bn gross cash stripped from the flows and the net cash added once in the bridge, leases as debt, EUR-built 8.5% WACC applied uniformly, terminal value the lower of Gordon (2.5%) and 18x year-10 owner FCF, three component-built scenarios weighted 25/50/25, and a 15% hurdle entry price with its terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle. The valuation is deliberately anchored to reported EBIT rather than Airbus's EBIT Adjusted because the recurring adjustments (dollar hedge revaluation, A400M, Space) are real costs. The street-basis memo differs little from house because SBC is only 0.45% of revenue.
key_risks_to_valuation: Engine supply (Pratt & Whitney GTF durability, CFM LEAP capacity) is the single largest swing factor for FY2026-27 deliveries, revenue and the H2-weighted cash flow; a miss on ~870 moves Y1 FCF by EUR 1bn+
Terminal value is ~60% of enterprise value and the Gordon formula binds at 8.5%/2.5%; each 50bp of WACC is worth roughly EUR 15-20/share (see sensitivity grid)
EUR/USD: >75% of revenue is dollar-denominated against euro costs with ~60% natural hedge; a 10c stronger euro on the unhedged book is ~EUR 1bn of EBIT
European Governments' refundable advances (EUR 3.8bn) are not treated as debt, following Airbus; treating them as debt would reduce value by ~EUR 4.8/share
Defence & Space and A400M programme charges have recurred (EUR 1.3bn Space charge FY2024); the base assumes they fade to a normal run-rate, which is the history's exception not its rule

Working capital is modelled neutral in the base; a sustained inventory build (gliders awaiting engines) or a drop in PDP inflows as book-to-bill falls to 1 would cut FCF by several hundred million a year
Price anchor predates the 28 Oct 2026 Q3/9M print; the balance-sheet anchor is the seasonally weak June 2026 position (post EUR 2.5bn dividend, pre H2 cash generation)
Cash tax is assumed to normalise to 24%; if deferred-tax assets last longer the base is conservative by ~EUR 400m/yr in the early years

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 consolidated statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payment (IFRS 2)' EUR 333m (AIR.PA_Annual_FY2025_FinancialStatements.txt:4569); equity-settled performance shares only, no separate equity-award tax line is disclosed so the combined figure equals the IFRS 2 charge
inputs.share_count_basis: 789,860,128 diluted weighted-average shares, H1 2026 interim note 13 (AIR.PA_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:1050); 787.2m outstanding at 31 Dec 2025 (792.3m issued less 5.1m treasury). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows and FY2025 buybacks of EUR 565m more than covered the 0.7m-share annual dilution, so the flat count is funded, not a convention
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:37:44Z regular close (Euronext Paris, Friday); Q3/9M 2026 results due 28 Oct 2026 -- refresh after that print
inputs.net_debt_basis: Airbus's own 'Net cash' definition at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 note 21): cash 9,499 + current securities 2,795 + non-current securities 11,082 = gross cash 23,376, less financing liabilities 14,276 (bonds/CP, bank, lease liabilities 2,425, other) less interest-rate contracts 740 = net cash 8,360. total_debt here = 14,276 + 740 so that total_debt - cash ties to net_debt. European Governments' refundable advances (EUR 3,822m at FY2025) are NOT treated as debt, matching Airbus's convention: they are repaid per delivery inside operating cash flow and refinanced by new advances; treating them as debt would cost ~EUR 4.8/share and is listed as a risk, not applied
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows discounted at an EUR-built rate: 10y Bund ~2.7% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.05 = cost of equity ~8.5%. Airbus carries net cash, so the capital structure is effectively all-equity and WACC = cost of equity = 8.5%. Same rate in all three scenarios: cyclicality, engine-supply and programme risk are charged once, in the flows and the weights, not stacked in the discount rate
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: IFRS 16 lease liabilities (EUR 2,425m at 30 Jun 2026) are inside financing liabilities and therefore inside net debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows. Ongoing right-of-use renewal (ROU additions EUR 942m FY2025, EUR 438m FY2024; ROU depreciation ~0.4% of revenue) is charged via ~0.5pp of revenue added to the capex path, so capex_pct = reported capex % + 0.5pp
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI book value EUR 88m (30 Jun 2026) deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are 100% consolidated. Airbus states the NCI have no material interest in cash flows
inputs.equity_method_treatment: Investments accounted for under the equity method (MBDA 37.5%, ATR 50%, ArianeGroup 50%; book EUR 2,360m at FY2025) are NOT added to the bridge because Airbus's EBIT definition already includes the share of their profit (EUR 305m FY2025) and the EBITDA margin path is anchored to that EBIT -- income in flows, asset out of bridge, never both
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials'), with owner-fcf-adaptations.md applied (EUR WACC, lease treatment A, NCI, matching-asset rule, risk charged once). Airbus is an aerospace manufacturer; it is not a bank, REIT or holdco, and its securities portfolio is treasury cash, not an investment business. OWNER FCF ANCHOR: reported FCF (OCF 7,995 - capex 3,964) 4,031 - SBC 333 - interest income 710 = 2,988; interest paid (651) remains inside OCF so this anchor is ~EUR 650m conservative vs a fully unlevered figure -- immaterial for the valuation because the projection is built from pre-interest EBITDA, not from last_fcf. EBITDA ANCHOR: FY2025 reported EBIT 6,082 + D&A 3,133 = 9,215 (12.55%); IFRS 2 SBC of 333 is expensed inside that EBIT, so the engine's pre-SBC adj. EBITDA margin for FY0 is 13.0% and sbc_pct 0.45% brings it back. Airbus's headline EBIT Adjusted (FY2024 5,354 vs reported 5,304; FY2025 not captured in core_metrics) is not used as the anchor: the recurring 'adjustments' (dollar PDP mismatch/hedge revaluation, A400M and Space charges) are real costs of running this business. FY2026 guidance (~870 deliveries, EBIT Adjusted ~EUR 7.5bn, FCF before customer financing ~EUR 4.5bn, reaffirmed 29 Jul 2026) informs year 1. COMPONENT CHECK on FY2025 actuals: EBITDA 9,215 - cash tax 965 - capex 3,964 = 4,286 vs reported OCF-capex 4,031 (gap = refundable-advance repayments, provisions, WC), so the component build reproduces the actual within ~6%. PERIOD CONSISTENCY: Y1 is full-year FY2026 while net cash is at 30 Jun 2026, so the H1 2026 reported FCF of -1,498 would be counted twice (once inside the June net cash, once inside Y1); the equity bridge reverses it. The EUR 2,530m FY2025 dividend paid in April 2026 is correctly excluded from a buyer's value today because the June balance sheet is post-payment. Lumpy historical FCF (customer financing, PDP timing, 2020 trough of -7.1bn) is why the base is a component build from EBITDA rather than any single year's FCF margin.

bear.narrative: Engines do not arrive: GTF durability and LEAP capacity cap FY2026 deliveries near 840 (revenue +6% with FX against), 'gliders' sit on the ramp, and rate 75 slips to 2028-29 so FY2027 grows only 3%. Fixed-cost under-absorption and tariff/FX drag hold pre-SBC EBITDA at ~12.6-13.5% (EBIT ~8.7%); Space and A400M generate further charges; COMAC's C919 takes the Chinese single-aisle market from 2030, so terminal growth is 2.0%. Inventory keeps absorbing cash (-10% of revenue growth), capex stays elevated at the Spirit sites, and interest-rate normalisation lowers treasury income (already stripped). No solvency risk: EUR 8bn net cash covers the path, so the bear case is value erosion, not distress.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +9%: ~870 deliveries (+9.7%) less an EUR/USD headwind on the unhedged ~40% of dollar revenue (H1 2026 was +12%). FY2027-28: A320-family rate 75 and A350 rate 12 reached, deliveries ~930-990, +7.5%/+6.5%. Then decay toward 2.5% as the ramp completes and growth reverts to traffic (Airbus GMF 3.6% traffic CAGR) less price.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA from 13.0% (FY2025) to 15.5% by FY2032: equivalent to EBIT ~10.8% of revenue, consistent with FY2026 guidance (EBIT Adj ~7.5bn on ~80bn = 9.4% pre-adjustments) plus operating leverage on fixed-cost final assembly, services mix (Unical, MRO), and Defence & Space restored to mid-single-digit margins post adaptation plan. Does not assume Boeing-share capture beyond the current backlog.
base.capex_rationale: Reported capex 5.4% of revenue (FY2025, EUR 3,964m incl. capitalised development and Spirit-site integration) + 0.5pp ROU lease renewal = 5.9% in Y1, gliding to 4.9% (4.4% reported + 0.5pp) once the rate-75 industrial system is in place. D&A 4.3% -> 4.2%.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 cash tax 965 on EBIT 6,082 = 15.9% vs 21.9% book ETR: deferred-tax assets (2019-20 losses, tax credits) are being consumed. Ramp cash rate from 17% to a 24% blended statutory rate (France 25.8%, Germany ~30%, Spain/NL ~25%, UK 25%) by Y8.
base.wc_rationale: Neutral. Airbus's working capital nets large inventories (~EUR 40bn) against larger customer advances/contract liabilities; with book-to-bill ~1.1 the PDP inflow roughly funds inventory growth. The FY2026 inventory build (engine shortage) is a Y1 timing effect inside the guidance, not a structural capture rate.

bull.narrative: Engines arrive: Pratt & Whitney and CFM meet 2026-27 volumes, deliveries hit the top of the 870 +/-20 range and run to ~1,000 by 2028 as rate 75 lands on schedule; A321XLR and A350F take share from Boeing's delayed MAX 10/777X; European rearmament lifts Defence & Space to a 7-8% margin and the Thales/Leonardo space JV removes the loss-making satellite tail; services and Unical push group pre-SBC EBITDA to 17% (EBIT ~12.4%). Growing backlog PDPs (book-to-bill >1.2) make working capital a modest cash source (+5% of revenue growth).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the binding constraint on FY2026-27 output (engine deliveries from two suppliers) is outside Airbus's control, H1 2026 FCF was -EUR 1.5bn with the whole year's cash and ~520 deliveries loaded into H2, and Q3 results land on 28 Oct 2026. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs rate 75 on time, 17% EBITDA and a benign dollar simultaneously, three things that have not co-occurred since 2019. Base 50%: the backlog makes the demand side close to certain; the dispute is pace and margin.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
